question.text: Sahyadri Stat-Arb enters at z = +2 (spread = INR 7.40) with INR 10 cr LONG in Stock Q and INR 10 cr SHORT in Stock P. Spread reverts to mean INR 5.00 (z=0). Assuming the INR 2.40 spread compression translates linearly to combined pair P&L of INR 2.40 lakh per INR 10 cr pair leg (illustrative), what is the GROSS P&L on the pair?

explanation.text: The Logic: Applying the stem's stated linear conversion (INR 2.40 lakh of combined pair P&L per INR 10 cr pair leg for each INR 1 of spread compression — phrased per the problem), the spread move from INR 7.40 to INR 5.00 is a compression of INR 2.40, giving a gross pair P&L of INR 2.40 lakh on the INR 10 cr long / INR 10 cr short pair. Both legs contribute when the spread converges toward its mean (the long-cheap leg appreciates and the short-rich leg falls). The Trap: Options A, C, and D misapply the stem's linear conversion or scale it incorrectly. The framing reflects general industry practice in statistical-arbitrage pair trading.
